subject: kraken
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: kraken rising, tentacles spread.
Style: Overwatch.
reasoning:
I'm sketching the design plan for a rising kraken creature with a mantle head, beak, and eight radiating tentacles with suckers, aiming for a stylized Overwatch-like palette of teal and purple with orange glow accents, and roughly sketching out realistic proportions for its scale.

Now I'm working out the skeleton: a root body joint with a mantle chain sweeping upward and back, eyes and a hinged beak at the front, and eight tentacles spaced radially around the body, each defined by a curving path of points that rises from the body, arcs down, and lies along the ground with the tips slightly curled.

Now I'm planning the undershade coloring with a cream belly sector and adding suckers along each tentacle's underside using small cylinders scaled by radius, placing about 7 per tentacle across all 8 limbs.

I'm also adding small orange spike accents along the top of each tentacle for an Overwatch-style look, then shifting to construct the mantle as a chain of joints rising from the body, naming each segment mantle1 through the tip and parenting the whole chain to the root body joint.

Setting up the mantle sweep with a smoothly tapering radius profile ending in a rounded point, then defining the skin paint as a mottled purple-teal pattern with a lighter countershaded belly tone.

Now adding two leaf-shaped fins extruded sideways near the back of the mantle, positioned symmetrically and oriented flat to stick outward from the body.

For the head, I'm placing an ellipsoid-scaled sphere above the mantle for the skull, then locating eye positions on its surface at symmetric azimuth/elevation angles to apply glowing slit-pupil decals, Overwatch-style.

I'll design the eye texture as a circular orange-yellow iris with a black slit pupil, white highlight, and dark lid rim, keeping the decal background transparent outside the circle. Above each eye I'm sticking a flattened, scaled sphere in a darker body tone to form a brow ridge, and now I'm working out the beak shape as a curved, hooked form swept below the head joint.

Setting up the jaw and upper beak joints with bezier sweeps to create a hooked, curved beak shape, colored dark with a cream bone-toned tip for an Overwatch-style look -- skipping extra tentacles or teeth since the beak alone should suffice.

Now I'm adding bioluminescent glow spots scattered across the mantle surface using glowing orange spheres, and giving the eye decals a subtle glow too since the texture material should handle it fine. For the mantle spots, I'm scattering spheres across the mantle's surface with minimum distance constraints for even placement.

I'm considering a ridge of orange spikes along the mantle's top but deciding to skip extra barnacle or coral details and the collar of spikes to keep things simpler. For stability I'm checking that the lowest points, like tentacle tips and body bottom, are close enough to the floor without sinking more than the allowed 2% tolerance.

Adjusting the radius and height coordinates further so the tentacle tapers smoothly toward the ground without dipping below zero, tweaking the knot positions to avoid an overly steep drop near the base.

I'm adding a lateral curl to the tentacle tips using perpendicular offsets, distributing eight tentacles evenly around the body at staggered angles so they don't cluster directly behind, and anchoring their roots inside the head so the joints stay hidden. For coloring, I'm planning a mottled countershaded purple pattern for the tentacles.

I'll skip the bands approach since its semantics are ambiguous, and instead use a gradient along the tentacle path to blend into orange near the tip, then apply the sweep with the computed color and belly sectors.

For the suckers, I'm placing small cylinder geometries along each tentacle using scale based on local radius, colored pale pink, keeping it simple without extra ring detailing for now.

Then I'm planning orange dorsal spikes along the upper part of each tentacle near the base, using a seeded random for sway and scatter, and sketching out the mantle's shape as a catmull curve chain with three segments building outward and upward.

Working out the fin geometry...

For the eye decal I'm attaching it to the head part using the hit normal for orientation, and building the head as a scaled sphere positioned forward on the body with countershaded body paint.

Now I'm placing brow bumps at symmetric angles on the head using a flattened, scaled sphere shape, and sketching out a ring of crest spikes near where the head meets the mantle.

Positioning the collar spikes around the back half of the head, adjusting radius so they sit snugly against the head's curvature without poking through the mantle. Once the beak details are settled I'll finalize the code, including glow imports and a filter for mantle spot placement based on surface normal.

Now sketching the eye as SVG: a dark outer ring, golden iris, vertical slit pupil, a highlight dot for glossiness, and an upper eyelid path shading the top portion for a more reptilian look.
